subject: Re: Encord <> Iterative | Active Trail Check-In
text:
Hi Shivant,

Thank you for reaching out! I truly appreciate the effort that your team
and, especially, Diarmuid put into organizing the trial.

After my trial and our discussion last week, I've come to the conclusion
that our use case for Active is currently quite limited. Initially, we
intended to use Active for comparing various models and their ground truth
at the video level. However, as Diarmuid mentioned, it appears that
Annotate from Encord would serve this purpose without needing to utilize
the Active feature. While we can use this approach, it also means we would
miss out on some valuable functionalities that Active offers, such as
ground truth comparisons. Unfortunately, some features in Active, like
thresholding, aren't applicable to our current model since the outputs lack
associated scores.

With the upcoming submission of the new SKOUT version, I suggested in our
last meeting that we explore more effective ways to integrate Active into
our workflow for this next release.

Once again, thank you for your time and support.

Best regards,
Evan

subject: Re: Encord and Presien
text:
Hi James and Yianni,

Here's a breakdown of our current approach to MLOPs at Presien.
I've attached a diagram of our pipeline, plus a table explaining each bit
and tried to highlight the bits that are currently sticking points for us.
These are primarily:

   - Recurring error identification
      - We do Active Learnign to get general errors and "Reactive-Learning"
      based on identifying potential FPs (primarily led by our customers plus
      some automation) but finding recurring patterns in both FPs and FNs is
      tricky
      - FPs we have a manual UI we have developed for visually sorting
      alerts into common issue groups
      - FNs we heavily rely on our AL pipeline, without having a good
      ability to detect recurring ones, over that through customer feedback and
      our own deployment testing. When we do spot a FN error, we will try and
      recreate it, but we do not have a good way of scanning our data for these
      other than simple image-feature searches (we are looking into using
      metadata, eg vehicle motion as well)
   - Creation and maintenance of regression tests from the above

I remember us chatting about maybe sending you some example data from our
pipeline, is this something you will need for the demo? I'll have to check
what we can send if so.

Let me know if you have any questions, otherwise I'm looking forward to
Monday.

*Stuart Eiffert*
Lead AI Engineer

Eveleigh NSW 2015

subject: RE: [EXTERNAL]  Re: Encord/Ideko – Ultrasonic Defect Detection
text:
Hi Alex,
Thank you again for your time. It was very helpful to better understand the possibilities of using Encord’s platform for ultrasonic inspection data.
I’m adding Jose Luis Lanzagorta to the loop. He is responsible for the NDT group at IDEKO.
To summarize our discussion:

  *
The meeting was a follow-up to explore potential collaboration around ultrasonic defect detection.
  *
IDEKO is interested in starting with a small-scale proof-of-concept within a research setting, not for immediate deployment to customers.
  *
The aim is to evaluate the added value ENCORD could bring when combined with IDEKOs data and expertise, as a way to demonstrate potential impact to our end users.
  *
We discussed a tentative budget of around €5,000 for this initial trial. We understand from your side that this is below your usual pricing model, though there might be internal options or discounts available for research centers.
  *
You mentioned that some partners begin with open-source workflows to demonstrate initial value before scaling up to Encord’s enterprise solution.

Next steps:
We’d appreciate it if you could explore internally whether there’s a feasible pricing model that could support our research objectives in the short term.
Thanks again — we remain very interested in collaborating, and we hope we can find a way to work together.
Best regards,
Julen
